text.title: Spec Delta Verb Routing
text.summary: Routing for ONE change. Run it per change, not per feature. The first two branches are the cases where the answer is that there is no delta to write.

decision-tree.root-question: For this one change: does it alter the durable shape of the system as recorded in `project-spec/`, and if so, which of the four verbs describes it?

conclusion.verdict: STOP. There is no baseline, so there is no delta. Write the full spec.md and adopt sdd/project-spec-structure first — a delta against nothing is a spec with confusing headings.

STOP. No delta. Refactors, dependency bumps and performance work do not change the durable shape of the system. If a reviewer disagrees, the disagreement is about whether project-spec/ was recording implementation detail it should not have been.

RENAMED, with an explicit `old -> new` pair in the block heading. Never a REMOVED plus an ADDED — that form loses every reference to the old identifier and neither a reader nor a tool can tell it was one operation. If the wording changes too, the RENAMED lands first and a separate CHANGED block addresses the post-rename name.

REMOVED — and the block MUST enumerate every acceptance criterion, requirement id, test file and user flow that referenced it, each with a new home or an explicit reason it is obsolete. `none` is allowed and must be verified with a search, not assumed.
CHANGED, with **Was:** and **Now:** lines and a **Scenarios:** line. Quote at most one line of the baseline for context; reproducing the section forks the source of truth.

Not a delta. A clarification that changes nothing about what is permitted is an edit to project-spec/ on its own, not an operation. Inventing a CLARIFIED verb to record it is how the closed vocabulary starts leaking.

ADDED, last in the file and last in application. Head the block with the new identifier. If that identifier collides with something after the first three operations have been applied, it is a genuine collision — resolve it, do not work around it by renaming the new thing.

`## Out of Scope`, one line, with the reason. Do NOT open an `## Unchanged` section — that set is the complement of the delta over the whole baseline, so it can never be complete and its incompleteness is indistinguishable from an oversight.

Overlay: only one pairing is legal — a RENAMED followed by a CHANGED on the same id. Anything else (added then changed, changed then removed) is a contradiction that reads as reasonable when the two blocks are eighty lines apart. Collapse it into one operation.

Do not archive. Merge into project-spec/ in the same pull request, run the project's acceptance check, and archive only after it passes. The delta is the instruction set you need to diagnose an incoherent merge, and archiving discards it exactly when it becomes valuable.
